correctness.rationale: For all n≥2 and positive real a_j, Jacobi irreducibility ensures simple real spectrum. Direct eigenvector recurrence gives polynomials in z² of degrees 0..n−1, establishing rank as the number of distinct squared eigenvalues. Residue and trailing/leading continuant-resultant products rigorously yield det(M)=(L/D0)τ^(2⌊n/2⌋)/Disc(χτ), with nonvanishing Δ. Positive definiteness follows for τ≠0; bipartite ± pairing gives rank ceil(n/2) at τ=0. Independently reconstructed rational Gram matrices verify determinant/rank for 48 small cases (finite corroboration only). Signs, normalization, n=2 boundary and negative τ have been checked.

evidence: Coutinho et al. (2018) develop the commutant/trace-projection representation, applicable to general symmetric Hamiltonians.
Coutinho et al., arXiv:2208.08971, give general exact methods for integral Hamiltonians.
Eisenberg et al., arXiv:1804.01645, use potentials for asymmetric state transfer, not average-mixing rank.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General projector and Gram identities can compute any finite instance, but do not by themselves determine the all-length family or explicit resultant discriminant ratio. The positive definiteness of a Jacobi Hamiltonian under any nonzero endpoint site perturbation is not a corollary of the cited zero-diagonal bipartite rank bound, because that hypothesis fails.
searches: doi:10.37236/7867 commutant rank and Gram framework

evidence: The zero-field rank is a weighted extension of a phenomenon explicit for unweighted paths in arXiv:1103.2578.
The field-dependent result uses new opposite-root resultants to derive a determinant not stated in the general spectral-projector literature.
The weighted-path transfer articles ask for transfer fidelity at selected times rather than long-time probability averages.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new claim is not a restatement of the τ=0 path rank, a two-endpoint loop perturbation, or a generic finite computation. In particular, generic simplicity of eigenvalues alone does not guarantee invertibility of their squared-eigenvector matrix. The essential new step is proving that all squared eigenvalues are distinct exactly when a single endpoint field is nonzero and computing the resulting Gram determinant. A broad unlocated theorem on Jacobi-square eigenvectors could still dominate the claim.

evidence: Godsil, arXiv:1103.2578, has path formula at zero field and examples with equal loops on both path endpoints.
Kirkland et al., arXiv:1708.03283, handle weighted tridiagonal potentials, but theorems in Sections 4–5 concern perfect state transfer.
No inspected source supplies a one-endpoint field determinant, its order of vanishing, or rank equality for all positive couplings.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalence tests included single-end loop versus double-end loops, eigenvector-square (orthostochastic) determinant and Jacobi polynomial recurrences. The double-end loop setting retains reflection symmetry and cannot imply the full-rank single-end conclusion. The present claim concerns a Cesaro Gram matrix, not transition amplitude or transfer fidelity.

evidence: The unperturbed path matrix is explicitly tabulated by Godsil, including its reflection rank defect.
Kirkland and van Bommel, arXiv:2112.02369, consider matching loops at both endpoints and quantify state transfer fidelity; they do not present the one-endpoint mixing determinant.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Known finite examples or tables of unweighted or two-endpoint paths do not provide the nonzero-potential weighted path determinant as a function of arbitrary edge couplings, order and real potential. No known exact database row was identified with the claim; an undiscovered table remains possible.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary literature gives Cesaro projector and commutant formulas, a zero-field unweighted path formula, weighted-path orthogonal polynomial recurrences for state transfer, and symmetric two-endpoint loop fidelity. Direct scientific implication comparison found none stating or immediately implying the all-coupling, all-order one-endpoint rank transition and discriminant determinant. A stronger unlocated Jacobi theorem remains a documented residual risk.
residual_risks: An implicit Jacobi eigenvector-square determinant in broader orthogonal-polynomial literature could subsume the theorem.
The entire 28-page two-endpoint-loop paper was not read line by line; although its inspected claims address different quantities, unexpected Cesaro appendices cannot be absolutely ruled out.
Semantic and keyword search, even combined with primary full-text inspection, cannot certify exhaustive novelty.

value.rationale: This gives a universal, sharp and physically motivated one-site symmetry-breaking threshold for long-time transport statistics on weighted spin chains, in every length and for arbitrary positive couplings. The exact discriminant formula quantifies determinant decay near the transition and is substantially stronger than a routine small example. Generic spectral simplicity alone does not explain full Gram rank; the resulting structural law requires nontrivial resultant analysis. No general downstream theorem is presumed.
